_comment: Classifies the 11 negative golden-set rows (empty Card IDs) into the two kinds
the PRD (§Evaluation) and DECISIONS-Explain-This.md score separately: true_gap
(no card exists for anything the sentence turns on) vs false_friend (a content
word IS a shelf card title/alias, but this sentence uses a different sense).
Method: mechanical, not eyeballed. For each row's sentence, normalise it
(lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) the same way
explain/index.js's normalise() does, then look for any shelf card title or
alias appearing as a whole-token match — i.e. the exact word-boundary rule
explain/retrieve.js's lexicalLeg() uses, including its MIN_SURFACE_CHARS=3
floor (a 1-2 char surface, e.g. the alias 'ai', never counts as a match).
A row with at least one such hit is false_friend; a row with none is
true_gap. Checked against shelf/shelf-export.json, version shelf-1010-02e436fd8106.
This mechanical check is a proxy for 'different sense', not a semantic judge —
row 27 is a genuine edge case where the hit is arguably the SAME sense; see
its reason for why it's still filed here rather than as a true_gap.

rows.sentence: Young people should vote for younger representatives who have a skin-in-the-game for our country's future.
rows.reason: No content word (skin-in-the-game, representatives, vote, younger) matches any shelf card title or alias. Plain civics sentence; nothing on the shelf is even adjacent.

rows.sentence: After helping design and build our Horizon AI incubator last year, I'm excited to officially take on the role of AI Enablement Strategist!
rows.reason: "AI" is technically an alias of the artificialintelligence card, but at 2 characters it sits below the lexical leg's MIN_SURFACE_CHARS=3 floor (explain/retrieve.js) and never fires as a match. No other word hits. Filed as true_gap because the mechanical check the harness actually runs finds nothing — consistent with the gold explanation ("AI" here is a program name and job title, not the concept).

rows.sentence: You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to be technically credible enough to make good build-vs-buy decisions, spot architectural risks early, and earn respect from a strong engineering team.
rows.reason: "spot" (as in "spot architectural risks") is a whole-word match against the alias "spot" on the spotinstances card (Spot instances — interruptible cloud compute). The sentence uses "spot" as an ordinary verb (notice), not the cloud-pricing sense.

rows.sentence: The Joker in Batman universe is portrayed as an agent of chaos, mastermind but also as a person who spoils people for fun.
rows.reason: "agent" matches the alias "agent" on the agents card. This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend ("agent of chaos" — the everyday sense, not an AI agent).

rows.sentence: Semantic Analysis is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that attempts to understand the meaning of Natural Language.
rows.reason: EDGE CASE, flagged rather than quietly filed. "NLP" and "Natural Language Processing" both hit the nlp card's title/alias, and here they name the actual NLP field — arguably the SAME sense the card covers, not a different one, so this doesn't cleanly fit the PRD's false-friend definition. The gold explanation ("the shelf doesn't cover 'semantic analysis' or NLP yet") reads as if it predates the shelf's nlp card, which exists in the current export (shelf-1010-02e436fd8106) with definition + examples. "Semantic Analysis" itself, the sentence's actual subject, has no shelf hit at all. Net effect: retrieval will very likely return the nlp card here, which the golden set's empty Card IDs will score as a leak — filed as false_friend (not true_gap) so that leak lands in the class where a leak is an expected, visible number rather than silently miscounted against true-gap coverage. Worth flagging to whoever maintains the golden set: either the shelf grew past this row's assumption, or the row should score card [nlp] as expected rather than none.

rows.sentence: Poshak alerted me of his father's death.
rows.reason: No content word matches any shelf card title or alias. Personal message, no AI content at all.

rows.sentence: In sexual harassment and misconduct cases, establishing whether consent was present, absent, or legally invalid is the fundamental standard for determining accountability, distinguishing unwelcome behavior from mutual interaction.
rows.reason: "consent" matches the consent card (data/informed consent in AI) and "accountability" matches the accountability card. This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (consent in the legal sense, not the AI-governance sense).

rows.sentence: What I saw on the weather dashboard was harrowing: the storm was traveling in the same direction.
rows.reason: "dashboard" matches the dashboards card (a UI pattern for monitoring model/agent metrics). The sentence uses it as an ordinary weather display, not the AI-monitoring sense.

rows.sentence: As a college dropout, he struggled to get a job.
rows.reason: "dropout" matches the dropout card (the regularization technique). This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (leaving college, not the ML regularizer).

rows.sentence: In chronology and periodization, an epoch or reference epoch is an instant in time chosen as the origin of a particular calendar era.
rows.reason: "epoch" matches the epoch card (one full pass over the training data). This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (the calendar-era sense, not the ML-training sense).

rows.sentence: His last five movies were all flops.
rows.reason: "flops" matches the flops card (floating point operations, a compute-cost unit). The sentence uses it as ordinary slang for failed films, not the FLOPs sense.
